title: Typed shared-edge encoder with joint action and motion diffusion
coverage_gap: Two short successful episodes couple object_x and goal_x and do not identify all causal stage transitions from raw marginals. The same nearby hand-object configuration can occur while approaching or lifting, and the dataset has little lateral goal-relative action variation. There is enough within-episode motion to supervise whether hand and object move together, without acquiring extra demonstrations.
reusable_regularity: A shared small MLP encodes four typed directed relations separately: hand-to-object, object-to-goal, hand-to-wall, object-to-wall. It sees relative displacement, distance, relative motion, aperture and native obstacle clearances. The acquisition edge has no goal endpoint; the transport edge explicitly uses the independent current goal. Concatenated role-specific embeddings let the single DP compose these relations. Jointly diffusing future hand displacement, object displacement and aperture with action4 encourages a latent contact/motion structure without hand-written stage gates. It is a learned relational and predictive-supervision prior, not the action chart of A2 or the fixed feature-only policy of A1.
dependencies_preserved: 31 ungated metric bypass channels retain world wall center, size, hand/object/goal wall-relative positions, both object xyzw quaternions, current/previous aperture and hand/object increments. All relevant current/previous physical poses remain reconstructible; only absent object2 channels are omitted.

The edge coordinates and actions remain in native world axes. World gravity, finite wall dimensions, signed native box-face offsets and top clearances remain explicit. No obstacle-independent rotational or reflection invariance is assumed.
The four edge roles remain distinct after a weight-shared encoder, rather than being pooled into an unordered average. The common U-Net learns their interactions and temporal behavior.

Inference condition receives only raw causal history. Auxiliary future channels are jointly generated diffusion variables, never future observations supplied to the inference condition. No predicted trajectory is passed to a planner or analytic controller; auxiliary channels are discarded by the public action decoder path.
evidence_refs: task_materials.json: native observation slices, object2 absence, native world action4 semantics, training/C/E factor splits
support_summary.json: 163 transitions; initial object-to-goal vectors and action marginal variability
trajectories/demo_00.json: obs rows 0-7 and 23-30 demonstrate stationary object during approach then object motion as the hand closes and lifts; actions rows 0-78 show multiple motion regimes
trajectories/demo_00.json: obs rows 48-51 show hand/object co-motion approaching the transport transition
trajectories/demo_01.json: obs rows 47-52 show simultaneous hand and object lift with nearly fixed separation
PUBLIC_CONTRACT.md, contracts.py, learning.py, diffusion_policy.py, language_policy.json and training_recipe.json
expected_failure_signature: If extra predicted-motion channels mostly memorize the two trajectories, the model may produce plausible lifts without the required lateral goal correction on C/E. If the auxiliary objective competes with action precision, grasp timing or closing may degrade despite plausible hand/object co-motion predictions. A learned encoder may overfit aperture or orientation traces rather than actual contact. These signatures are hypotheses, not observed outcomes.

required_runtime_fields.input: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45], using hand 0:3 and 18:21, aperture 3:4 and 21:22, object 4:7 and 22:25, xyzw quaternions 7:11 and 25:29, goal 36:39, wall center 39:42 and wall half size 42:45
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: 127 dimensions per observation: four 24-dimensional learned edge embeddings plus a 31-dimensional metric bypass. Each edge starts with 24 deterministic values including its four-way role. Shared MLP 24->64->24 with SiLU and LayerNorm. Every learned module is registered only in build_modules and participates in the joint optimizer loss.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity native world action4 is the first four diffusion channels. World xyz is measured in native 0.01 m/action units; gripper is unchanged. Host alone clips the decoded native cube and executes the fixed four-step prefix.
required_runtime_fields.deployment_state: No fitted statistics, label caches or training episode data are retained. The edge-role identity matrix is a registered checkpoint buffer. Common normalizer and optimizer settings are untouched; representation uses physical scales rather than support marginal normalization.

training_only_targets.name: future_motion
training_only_targets.source: Only exact D_N support episodes passed to training_targets. For window (episode,t), valid step k uses obs[t+k+1,0:3], obs[t+k+1,4:7], obs[t+k+1,3] and chunk-start obs[t]. No reward, success, expert source or environment internals.
training_only_targets.meaning: First three channels: future hand minus chunk-start hand in world meters / 0.10. Next three: future object minus chunk-start object / 0.10. Last: 2*(future aperture-0.5). Invalid padded future slots are zeros, not repeated terminal truth.
training_only_targets.use: Appended after unmodified encoded action4, producing diffusion_action_dim=11. Host-owned diffusion noise and the single common U-Net jointly model all channels. During inference all eleven channels are sampled/denoised without any future label lookup; only the first four are decoded as actions.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional 0.20 times auxiliary epsilon squared error, multiplied by the common valid transition mask and divided by 7*mask.sum() (safe denominator floor 1 for an empty mask). This normalization is separate from, and cannot change, the public weight-1 action epsilon loss denominator 4*mask.sum().

change_summary: Initial pre-feedback design. Introduces weight-shared learned typed-edge embeddings and seven joint motion/aperture diffusion channels with a separately normalized nonnegative auxiliary loss. Keeps native action frame, one unmodified factory U-Net, fixed action loss, history/horizon/execution prefix and all common training budgets. No explicit phase thresholds, support fitting, action prior controller, planner, pretrained encoder or extra demonstrations.
